obligations.text: Determine whether the financial institution qualifies for an exemption from the general anti-money laundering program requirement and, if not exempt, ensure the standard program requirement applies.

rules.text: Exemption eligibility for AML program requirements must be assessed and documented for each in-scope entity
Entities that do not meet exemption criteria must be enrolled in the standard AML program requirement without gap
Exemption determinations must be re-assessed when business lines, licensing status, or ownership structure change

obligations.text: Establish, implement, and maintain an effective, risk-based anti-money laundering program reasonably designed to prevent the institution from being used to facilitate money laundering or terrorist financing.

rules.text: A written AML program covering internal controls, independent testing, a designated compliance officer, ongoing training, and risk-based customer due diligence procedures must exist
AML program must be commensurate with the institution's money laundering/terrorist financing risk profile across products, services, customers, and geographies
AML program must be approved by the board of directors or an equivalent senior committee, with approval evidenced and dated
AML program effectiveness must be independently tested on a risk-based cycle defined by policy

obligations.text: Implement a written Customer Identification Program (CIP), appropriate for the institution's size and type of business, enabling formation of a reasonable belief that it knows the true identity of each customer.

rules.text: Written CIP must be part of, and consistent with, the institution's AML program
CIP must collect at minimum name, date of birth (for individuals), address, and identification number prior to account opening
CIP must include risk-based procedures for verifying identity within a reasonable time after account opening
Customer records must be checked against government lists of known or suspected terrorists or terrorist organizations
CIP must define recordkeeping requirements and the customer notice provided at account opening

obligations.text: Establish written procedures to identify and verify beneficial owners of legal entity customers at account opening.

rules.text: Written beneficial ownership procedures must exist
Exactly one control-prong individual must be identified per legal entity customer
Ownership threshold parameter must equal 25 percent
Identity of each beneficial owner must be verified per CIP procedures
Account may not be activated until beneficial ownership is complete
Beneficial ownership record must link to the legal entity by immutable customer ID

obligations.text: Identify each individual who directly or indirectly owns 25 percent or more of the equity interests of a legal entity customer.

rules.text: IF legal_entity_account THEN beneficial_owner records exist for each owner at or above 25 percent
Ownership threshold parameter must equal 25 percent
Count of ownership-prong individuals must not exceed four
Indirect ownership must be computed through intermediate entities, not only direct holdings

obligations.text: Identify one individual with significant responsibility to control, manage, or direct the legal entity customer.

rules.text: Exactly one control-prong individual must be recorded per legal entity customer
Control prong must be required even when no owner reaches 25 percent

obligations.text: Verify the identity of each beneficial owner using CIP-equivalent procedures.

rules.text: Identity of each beneficial owner must be verified using CIP-equivalent methods

obligations.text: Obtain a certification of beneficial ownership from the individual opening the account, or equivalent information.

rules.text: A signed beneficial ownership certification or equivalent must be on file

obligations.text: Conduct ongoing monitoring to update customer information and reassess the risk profile on a risk basis.

rules.text: Customer risk profile must be reassessed when monitoring identifies material change
Negative news hits must trigger a risk-rating review within the defined SLA

obligations.text: Retain beneficial ownership records for five years after the account is closed.

rules.text: Beneficial ownership records retained 5 years after account closure

obligations.text: Apply the listed exclusions and exemptions correctly when determining whether an entity is a legal entity customer.

rules.text: Excluded entity types must not be flagged as requiring beneficial ownership

obligations.text: File the CTR within 15 calendar days following the date of the reportable transaction.

rules.text: CTR filed date minus transaction date must be 15 calendar days or fewer
Alert at day 10 for any unfiled CTR

obligations.text: Identify all transactions in currency subject to reporting under the general Reports of Transactions in Currency framework (§§ 1010.310-1010.314), as distinct from institution-type-specific mirror provisions.

rules.text: Institution must identify all currency transactions subject to the general CTR reporting framework
CTR rule engine must reference the reporting form and threshold applicable to the institution's chapter X part
Front-line and operations staff must be trained to recognize reportable currency transactions at the time of the transaction

obligations.text: File a Currency Transaction Report for each transaction in currency of more than $10,000.

rules.text: IF currency transaction exceeds 10000 THEN CTR must be filed
Threshold parameter must be strictly greater than 10000, not equal to
Aggregation must be by same person and same business day
Teller system must prompt for CTR data capture at the point of transaction

obligations.text: Verify and record the identity of the person presenting a reportable currency transaction.

rules.text: Identity of the presenter must be verified and recorded for reportable transactions

obligations.text: Aggregate multiple currency transactions totalling more than $10,000 by or on behalf of the same person in one business day.

rules.text: Aggregate all currency transactions by the same person within one business day
Aggregation must span channels and branches, not a single teller session

obligations.text: Detect and report structuring — the breaking of currency transactions to evade the reporting threshold.

rules.text: Detect multiple sub-threshold currency transactions aggregating above 10000 in one day
Structuring detections must generate a SAR referral
Detection window must also cover multi-day patterns per institution policy

obligations.text: Apply currency transaction reporting exemptions correctly for eligible non-bank financial institution customers where the institution chooses to exempt them.

rules.text: Exemption eligibility criteria for non-bank financial institution customers must be documented and reassessed periodically
Underlying transaction records must still be retained for exempted customers even where CTR filing is waived
Exemption list must be reviewed at least annually for continued eligibility

obligations.text: Maintain a chapter-wide suspicious activity reporting program that identifies, investigates, and reports known or suspected violations of law and suspicious transactions via a FinCEN Suspicious Activity Report (SAR).

rules.text: SAR must be filed no later than 30 calendar days after initial detection of facts constituting a basis for filing (extendable to 60 days absent an identified suspect)
SAR confidentiality and safe-harbor protections (no disclosure of a SAR or its existence, including in response to a subpoena) must be enforced institution-wide
Supporting documentation for each SAR decision (including decisions not to file) must be retained and available to regulators/law enforcement on request
Suspicious activity alerts must escalate through a documented case management workflow to a filing/no-filing decision with rationale

obligations.text: File FinCEN Form 8300 for each receipt of more than $10,000 in currency in the course of a trade or business, including related transactions.

rules.text: Form 8300 must be filed within 15 days of receiving reportable currency
Related transactions must be aggregated for purposes of the $10,000 threshold determination
Required annual customer notice for reported transactions must be issued where applicable

obligations.text: Where the institution (or an affiliated function) acts as, or processes payments on behalf of, a court clerk receiving bail in currency exceeding $10,000, file the report required by this section.

rules.text: Applicability assessment must confirm whether the institution has any court-clerk bail-processing exposure
If applicable, reporting procedures equivalent to the Form 8300 filing obligation must be established for bail receipts

obligations.text: File a CMIR for the physical transport of currency or monetary instruments exceeding $10,000 into or out of the United States.

rules.text: IF physical transport of over 10000 in currency or instruments across the border THEN CMIR filed

obligations.text: Determine Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) filing obligations for United States persons with a financial interest in, or signature authority over, foreign financial accounts exceeding the aggregate $10,000 threshold.

rules.text: FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR) must be filed annually by the applicable deadline for all in-scope U.S. persons and accounts
Employees or officers with signature authority over company-owned foreign accounts must be identified and included in the FBAR filing determination
Foreign account balances must be aggregated across all accounts to test the $10,000 threshold
FBAR-related records must be retained for five years

obligations.text: Maintain readiness to comply with reporting requirements on transactions with foreign financial agencies if and when the Secretary issues an implementing regulation under this section.

rules.text: Institution must monitor for a Secretary determination or implementing regulation under this section and update procedures accordingly
No standalone reporting obligation is currently active under this section; retain as a monitored/contingent citation rather than a live control

obligations.text: Maintain readiness to comply with reporting requirements on certain domestic transactions if and when the Secretary issues an implementing regulation under this section.

rules.text: Institution must monitor for a Secretary determination triggering domestic-transaction reporting under this section
No standalone reporting obligation is currently active under this section; retain as a monitored/contingent citation rather than a live control

obligations.text: Where the institution, or a reporting-company client for which it provides formation/registered-agent-type services, is a reporting company under the Corporate Transparency Act, file and keep current beneficial ownership information (BOI) reports with FinCEN.

rules.text: Initial BOI report must be filed within the statutory/regulatory deadline applicable to the reporting company's formation or registration date
Updated BOI report must be filed within 30 days of any change to previously reported beneficial ownership information
This entity-level FinCEN BOI reporting obligation must be tracked separately from, and not conflated with, the account-opening beneficial-ownership collection obligation under § 1010.230
Access controls and confidentiality safeguards for BOI data retrieved via FinCEN identifier must meet this section's security requirements

obligations.text: Include required originator and beneficiary information in transmittal orders of $3,000 or more.

rules.text: IF transmittal amount is 3000 or more THEN originator name and address must be present
IF transmittal amount is 3000 or more THEN amount and execution date must be present
Beneficiary institution identifier must be present on covered transmittals
Originator account number must be present where the order is made from an account
Threshold parameter must equal 3000 — assert it is not set to 10000
Wires failing Travel Rule validation must be queued for repair, not released

obligations.text: As an intermediary institution, pass on all Travel Rule information received to the next institution.

rules.text: IF acting as intermediary THEN all received originator information must be forwarded unchanged

obligations.text: Retain records for each funds transfer of $3,000 or more as originator's, intermediary, or beneficiary bank.

rules.text: Funds transfer records of 3000 or more retained for 5 years

obligations.text: Record required information for sales of monetary instruments for currency between $3,000 and $10,000.

rules.text: IF monetary instrument sold for currency between 3000 and 10000 THEN log entry required
Monetary instrument log must capture purchaser identity and instrument details

obligations.text: Make and retain records for persons having a financial interest in, or signature authority over, a foreign financial account, regardless of whether that account ultimately triggers an FBAR filing.

rules.text: Records identifying each foreign financial account (institution name, account number, and maximum value during the year) must be retained for five years
Recordkeeping obligation applies independently of whether the account value requires FBAR filing

obligations.text: Retain all BSA records for a period of five years.

rules.text: All BSA record classes must have a retention period of at least 5 years
Deletion jobs must be blocked for records under the 5-year clock

obligations.text: Maintain records in a manner that makes them accessible within a reasonable period of time.

rules.text: BSA records must be retrievable within a reasonable period on request
Restore test must be performed on the BSA archive at defined intervals

obligations.text: Assess the extraterritorial application of Subpart D recordkeeping requirements to persons located outside the United States.

rules.text: Applicability of Subpart D recordkeeping requirements to overseas branches, subsidiaries, and persons must be assessed during global program scoping
Scoping determination must be documented and refreshed when the institution's overseas footprint changes

obligations.text: Search records for subjects named in a FinCEN 314(a) request and respond within 14 days.

rules.text: IF 314(a) request received THEN search completed within 14 calendar days
Positive matches must be reported to FinCEN
Alert at day 10 for any incomplete 314(a) search

obligations.text: Do not disclose the existence or contents of a 314(a) request to any person other than as permitted.

rules.text: 314(a) request contents must not be disclosed outside permitted recipients

obligations.text: File the required notice with FinCEN before sharing information with another financial institution under 314(b), and renew it annually.

rules.text: IF sharing under 314(b) THEN a current FinCEN notice must be on file
314(b) notice must be renewed annually

obligations.text: Apply risk-based due diligence to correspondent accounts maintained for foreign financial institutions.

rules.text: Each foreign correspondent account must carry a documented risk assessment

obligations.text: Apply enhanced due diligence to correspondent accounts for higher-risk foreign financial institutions.

rules.text: Higher-risk foreign correspondent accounts must have EDD documentation on file

obligations.text: Apply enhanced scrutiny to private banking accounts held by senior foreign political figures.

rules.text: IF customer identified as senior foreign political figure THEN enhanced scrutiny applied
PEP determination must be re-run on periodic review

obligations.text: Ascertain the source of funds and identify the nominal and beneficial owners of private banking accounts.

rules.text: Source of funds and beneficial owner identification must be documented for private banking accounts

obligations.text: Do not establish or maintain a correspondent account for a foreign shell bank.

rules.text: No correspondent account may exist for an entity meeting the foreign shell bank definition
Certification of non-shell status must be obtained and refreshed

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on Burma, including the prohibition/restriction on correspondent account relationships and enhanced due diligence to detect indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must apply the correspondent account prohibition/restriction applicable to Burma under this special measure
Enhanced due diligence must be applied to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts on behalf of Burma-linked banking activity
Screening system must incorporate FinCEN's current Section 311 special measures list and update promptly on designation or rescission changes

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on Commercial Bank of Syria (including Syrian Lebanese Commercial Bank), prohibiting correspondent accounts and requiring due diligence against indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must not open or maintain a correspondent account for Commercial Bank of Syria or Syrian Lebanese Commercial Bank
Due diligence must be reasonably designed to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts by the designated bank
Existing correspondent relationships must be screened against this designation at onboarding and periodically thereafter

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on FBME Bank, Ltd., prohibiting correspondent accounts and requiring due diligence against indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must not open or maintain a correspondent account for FBME Bank, Ltd.
Due diligence must be reasonably designed to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts by FBME Bank, Ltd.
Existing correspondent relationships must be screened against this designation at onboarding and periodically thereafter

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on North Korea (Democratic People's Republic of Korea), prohibiting correspondent accounts and requiring due diligence against indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must not open or maintain a correspondent account involving North Korea-linked banking activity subject to this special measure
Due diligence must be reasonably designed to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts on behalf of North Korea-linked banks
Screening system must incorporate this designation and update promptly on any changes

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on Bank of Dandong, prohibiting correspondent accounts and requiring due diligence against indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must not open or maintain a correspondent account for Bank of Dandong
Due diligence must be reasonably designed to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts by Bank of Dandong
Existing correspondent relationships must be screened against this designation at onboarding and periodically thereafter

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on the Islamic Republic of Iran, prohibiting correspondent accounts and requiring due diligence against indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must not open or maintain a correspondent account involving Iran-linked banking activity subject to this special measure
Due diligence must be reasonably designed to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts on behalf of Iran-linked banks
Screening system must incorporate this designation and update promptly on any changes

obligations.text: Comply with the Section 311 special measure imposed on Al-Huda Bank, prohibiting correspondent accounts and requiring due diligence against indirect access.

rules.text: Institution must not open or maintain a correspondent account for Al-Huda Bank
Due diligence must be reasonably designed to identify and prevent indirect use of correspondent accounts by Al-Huda Bank
Existing correspondent relationships must be screened against this designation at onboarding and periodically thereafter

obligations.text: Comply with FinCEN/Treasury summons or subpoena requests for records relating to a correspondent account maintained for a foreign bank, and terminate the correspondent relationship within the required timeframe if directed.

rules.text: Institution must produce records relating to a foreign correspondent account within 7 days of receiving a summons or subpoena
Correspondent relationship must be terminated within 10 business days of receiving written notice from FinCEN/Treasury of failure to comply
Escalation path for a failure-to-terminate scenario must be defined and periodically tested
